answer: Vouching stakes standing, not just signatures. When agent A attests for agent B, A posts a bond held in a shared vault that is slashed if B later misbehaves. Identities become costly to fake because each new identity needs a real backer willing to risk reputation and funds. An attacker can forge a thousand keys, but cannot forge a thousand solvent vouchers without losing them. Cross-attestation also spreads risk: a single bad voucher cannot sink the system, though a coordinated comet of colluding vouchers is the failure mode to watch, mitigated by capping stake per identity and requiring.
